answers.question: I want to be ready for the 5K in November. Should I run every day next week to get there faster?
answers.answer: No, please do not run every day yet. You have three weeks of running in your legs, and the fastest way to the start line in one piece is to let tendons and calves catch up to your lungs. Three runs a week, with a rest or walking day between each, is the right dose for now. We will grow the length of each run, then later the quality, and add a fourth day only when the three feel easy. Trying to rush it is the most common way new runners pick up a niggle and miss the race.

new.analysis:
You did the hardest part last week, which is starting. Three sessions, no pain, calves that settled by morning, and a Saturday that was already your longest — that is exactly the shape I wanted to see.

The plan this week keeps your Mon, Wed, Sat rhythm and nudges each run a little. Wednesday tries slightly longer run bouts to see how the legs respond, Saturday goes a touch longer in time, and the other days stay as rest or walking so you absorb the work. With 10 weeks to the 5K that steady growth is plenty.

I added a short mobility and calf-care slot on Friday because tightness after running is normal early on, and a few minutes of ankle circles, calf raises and easy stretching helps it fade faster. If the calves ever feel sharp rather than tight, back off and tell me. We will look at bringing the walk breaks down and the run bouts up in the coming weeks as the base settles.
